question:
The top and bottom bases of a rectangular prism are parallel. A lateral face has a line of intersection with each of these two bases. Are these two lines of intersection parallel? Answer 1 if they are parallel and 0 if they are not.

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_h119_q2_question_en.svg)
solution: The lateral face cuts a pair of parallel planes. The lines of intersection are two corresponding edges of the top and bottom bases, and they are parallel.

solutionMethods.explanation: The lateral face cuts a pair of parallel planes. The lines of intersection are two corresponding edges of the top and bottom bases, and they are parallel.
solutionMethods.label: Intersections with parallel planes

solutionMethods.explanation: Each lateral face is a rectangle, so we can reason within that face. In the front face \(ABCD\), the two intersection lines are \(AB\) and \(DC\). Since \(\angle DAB=\angle ADC=90^\circ\), these same-side interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\), giving \(AB\parallel DC\). The same argument applies to every lateral face, so the answer is \(1\).

reference.question:
The top and bottom bases of a rectangular prism are parallel. A lateral face has a line of intersection with each of these two bases. Are these two lines of intersection parallel? Answer 1 if they are parallel and 0 if they are not.

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_h119_q2_question_en.svg)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Intersections with parallel planes

The lateral face cuts a pair of parallel planes. The lines of intersection are two corresponding edges of the top and bottom bases, and they are parallel.

Method 2: Right angles in a lateral rectangle

Each lateral face is a rectangle, so we can reason within that face. In the front face \(ABCD\), the two intersection lines are \(AB\) and \(DC\). Since \(\angle DAB=\angle ADC=90^\circ\), these same-side interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\), giving \(AB\parallel DC\). The same argument applies to every lateral face, so the answer is \(1\).
